excerpt: 4 minutes LLMs have made bot programming boring, how can we make it fun again? If you’ve ever played codingame or any equivalent multiplayer bot programming contest, you know that it’s one of the most fun ways to program. Bot programming is competitive programming where you code programs (bots) that compete against other people’s bots to achieve some objective. But in recent years, with the onset of capable LLMs, people have been spamming Codingame with auto generated LLM solutions that, frankly, work quite well. I don’t really like this, since I really enjoyed (and still enjoy) the struggle of creating solutions on Codingame. I don’t do bot programming to create some external value (resume, etc.), I do it for the struggle and the urge to beat other human players. And I assume that a lot of people who do bot programming do it for a similar reason. Bot programming isn’t just about using algorithms to win, instead, it is about trying out different strategies to beat other players’ strategies. And when people use AI to brute force your algorithm/strategy, it gets boring because there is no longer an incentive to create new solutions, since you know someone can copy it to a degree by just throwing tokens at the problem with little to no effort. Top human written, creative solutions still beat these LLMs, but automated LLMs in loops are reaching fairly high levels of play, making it annoying for anyone who isn’t god level. So, how can we change this imbalance? Who am I? I am by no means one of the top players on Codingame or any other bot programming competition, but I have spent a large amount of my life playing these games on different platforms (I started when I was 8, and I am currently 18). This is just what I have observed and what I think will become of the entire bot programming space.
